title: The Rite of Spring / Mirror review – glitchy Stravinsky and digital doppelgangers from Alexander Whitley | Stage | The Guardian
summary: Mirror and The Rite of Spring by Alexander Whitley explore the tension between human performers and technology, with the latter often overshadowing the former. Both pieces feature digital effects and repetitive choreography, but the latter also incorporates Stravinsky's score and a sacrificial dance.
sentiment_reason: The articles describe a negative market impact due to the focus on technology over human elements, fears of repetitive choreography, and the lack of a clear positive outcome or breakthrough in the performances.
